notes: GR3 obliges one thing: DISABLE INPUT deactivates 'the logical paths between the queue and sub-queues specified by the contents of data-name-1 ... through data-name-4 ... and all the associated enabled sources'. Every probe, the reader's, the refuter's and mine, shows that done: the named structure and every level below it close against every source, a partly disabled structure has its remaining paths closed, and an unknown level takes no action. The refuter's question is about the STATUS KEY, which GR3 does not govern: Table 1 (via XIV.2.2.4 GR34 and GR1) does. On that question the text decides two things. (1) A partly disabled structure: the text gives no rule that makes DISABLE Q1 with S1 already closed and S2 open a 15. GR1 makes 15 the status of a statement whose specified source or destination 'is already disconnected', and the structure Q1 is not; the compiler answers 00 and closes S2, which conforms. (2) An unknown level below a known prefix that is already in the requested state: Table 1 marks 80 possible for the ENABLE INPUT and DISABLE INPUT columns and not for the TERMINAL forms, and §1985:B.2.2 (41) e says 80 is returned for an ENABLE or DISABLE 'where new communication status key condition 15 and communication status key condition 20 both apply'. For the INPUT form that can happen only when a referenced queue level is already disabled (B.2.2 (41) a: 'a queue ... referenced is already disabled') and a lower level is unknown. The compiler answers 20 there, so it never produces 80 for an INPUT statement. That is a defect, but of the status rule (XIV.2.2.4 GR34 / Table 1, and GR1's 'indicates this condition'), not of GR3: both 20 and 80 take no action, so what GR3 deactivates is the same under both readings. Charged to the sibling row below.
